title: Bounded witnesses for every continuous-variable entangled state
source: Sperling and Vogel prove this criterion for arbitrary-dimensional Hilbert spaces in Theorem 2 and Eq. (7) \sourcecite{ref:ser17-1}{SV09}.
progress: The answer is affirmative: Sperling--Vogel, Theorem 2, proves Eq.~\eqref{eq:ser17-statement-1} for every entangled density operator. Their Eq. (5) identifies the separable supremum with the pure-product supremum. The proof uses separation of a state from the trace-norm closed convex separable set by a bounded Hermitian functional. It also detects positive-partial-transpose entanglement \sourcecite{ref:ser17-1}{SV09}.

references.label: ref:ser17-1
references.tex: J. Sperling and W. Vogel, "Necessary and Sufficient Conditions for Bipartite Entanglement," \emph{Physical Review A} \textbf{79}, 022318 (2009). \href{https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.79.022318}{doi:10.1103/PhysRevA.79.022318}; \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/0805.1318}{arXiv:0805.1318}.

comment: The resolving result is peer-reviewed. Existence of a bounded witness does not supply an efficient finite-moment algorithm. Arbitrary density operators need not have all polynomial moments.
